topology.failover: manual promotion and regional BFF restart

checks.name: Region A login succeeds without exposing a JWT
Region B restores the Session created in Region A
Replica contains the encrypted Session before fault injection
Regional metrics are labelled and contain no account identifier
Region B continues authorization after Region A is stopped
Application-region RTO stays within the local objective
State-store outage returns 503 and never authorizes from stale process memory
Promoted TLS replica restores the pre-failure Session
Redis failover RTO stays within the local objective
Logout on the promoted region globally revokes the Session

limitations: Local Docker fault injection does not emulate WAN latency, DNS, quorum, or cloud control-plane delay.
Redis promotion is deliberately manual; production requires a managed or quorum-controlled failover mechanism.
The drill proves Session continuity and fail-closed authorization, not globally active-active Redis writes.
